author: abcoathup
content:
We need client teams to be able to log their preferences with the same definitions of priority. One tool, one scale. At the very least add the ability to save preferences and share them, even if just encoded in a URL. 

The prioritisation process for Glamsterdam was not great.  We need a single source of truth for shortlisted candidates. (Hopefully Forkcast).

author: wolovim
content: obvs intend to support the signaling and decision-making process as best i can, but im not advocating for mandating all teams use this. i think youre getting at something deeper/more upstream than this exercise though, re: prioritization

author: abcoathup
content:
There are two distinct tasks (apologies if I conflated) 

Team preferences and ACD shortlisting. 

Team preferences used a variety of ways to document. Several teams used Forkcast tiers but had different scales. See links to preferences: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/glamsterdam-upgrade-non-headliner-scoping-execution-layer/26502

It would be helpful to label the tiers so all teams were using the same scale. 

e.g. A = priority & achievable, B = secondary priority, C = nice to have, D = DFI (Geth used D for no)

This doesn’t mandate its use but it would make it much easier to collate team preferences.

Shortlisting is the second task which Forkcast can be the source of truth. 

For Glamsterdam there were multiple documents, including third party documents attempting to track combined preferences and shortlists. (Ansgar had the official list for EL, Christine and I both had our own independent lists. )

Using Forkcast (which is now great at tracking PFI) would provide a clear update of what was being considered.
